historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 guidance (mid-to-high single-digit aggregated revenue/EBITA growth), not a historical CAGR -- see notes
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All historical CAGRs (revenue, equity, owner-FCF) are dominated by the FY2019 Jacobs ECR acquisition step-change and the extreme FY2023 trough (EBITA margin 3.2%, EPS $0.07) / FY2025 peak (margin 6.8%, EPS $0.776) / FY2026 pullback (margin 6.1%, EPS $0.471) cycle, so none is a usable growth proxy. Equity CAGR is negative (-2.7% 5yr, -4.5% 3yr) purely because of buybacks ($166m+$359m) and dividends exceeding retained earnings plus AUD-strengthening FX translation losses, not operating decline -- FY2026 NPAT was still positive at $238m. EPS CAGRs (23-89%) are an artifact of the FY2023 trough denominator and are not meaningful either. selected_growth_rate is therefore taken from FY2027 management guidance plus the margin-recovery/backlog narrative (see historical_growth notes in inputs.notes), not from a mechanical CAGR -- this ticker needed a mid-cycle qualitative judgment, not the default equity-CAGR rule.

scenario_narratives.base: Backlog conversion and the FY2027 guided mid-to-high single-digit growth play out roughly as management describes, with margin normalizing from the FY2026 Middle-East-depressed trough back toward the historical average -- not all the way to the 9.0-9.5% ex-procurement ambition, which is treated as aspirational rather than base case.
scenario_narratives.bull: The FY2030 double-digit EBITA growth ambition is substantially achieved: Middle East resolves fast, North America and the major-projects pipeline (LNG, energy transition materials, data centers) convert at pace, and full-project-delivery plus AI/digital investment expand margin into management's target band.
scenario_narratives.bear: Middle East disruption and guidance misses recur, competitive EPCM tendering keeps margin structurally below its five-year average, and rising leverage combined with weaker operating cash flow slows the capital-return program -- growth stalls and the FY2025 margin peak is never regained.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Worley is valued on a 10-year component-built owner-FCF DCF, mid-cycle normalized off a FY2026 trough year rather than extrapolated from either the FY2025 peak or the FY2026 Middle-East-depressed result. The FY2019 Jacobs ECR acquisition roughly doubled the business and breaks any pre-2020 trend, so all growth and margin paths are anchored to FY2022-FY2026 history plus FY2027 guidance and the FY2030 medium-term ambition, discounted for the fact that management has twice revised the current year's guidance down within the same fiscal year.
key_risks_to_valuation: Middle East conflict duration and second-order supply chain effects (sulphur, delayed FIDs) beyond the FY2027 recovery management now expects
Guidance credibility -- the Middle East impact was upgraded from $30-40m to $60m mid-year, and FY2027 guidance replaces FY2026 guidance that was downgraded twice
Rising leverage (gearing 26.4% vs 20.9%) combined with nearly-halved operating cash flow while buybacks continued
AUD strength as a persistent translation headwind on predominantly USD/other-currency-denominated earnings, independent of operating performance
Structural margin ceiling from intense EPCM competition (Jacobs, Fluor, KBR, Bechtel, Wood Group) capping how far the 9.0-9.5% ex-procurement ambition can be realized

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report note 'Share based payments expense' (file:8931, $23m) and reconciliation table (file:7957/7991); tax withholding on vesting performance rights is settled by cancelling rights (file:7399/7624), not cash, so no separate equity-award cash-tax add is required — the $23m P&L expense is the full owner-FCF charge
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T06:10:11Z regular session (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 9.55-14.615
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-denominated flows and AUD-listed equity: ~4.2% 10yr ACGB risk-free + ~5.5-6% ERP x beta ~1.0-1.1 for a moderately cyclical, low-capital-intensity EPCM services business => ~9.5%. Consistent with other ASX cyclical industrials in this folder (BAP.AX 9.5%, BSL.AX 10.0%, ORI.AX 9.0%).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A (leases as debt). AASB16 lease liabilities ($242m FY2026: $84m current + $158m non-current) are included once, inside the company's own 'Net debt' definition ($1,746m = $2,611m interest-bearing borrowings ex-lease + $242m lease liabilities - $1,107m cash, per FY2026 Annual Report file:9472-9480). Lease principal repayments ($94m FY2026) sit in financing activities per the cash flow statement (file:8049) and are NOT deducted a second time from operating/free cash flow. No separate lease-interest disclosure exists to split from 'Net finance costs' ($108m), so Treatment B (lease payment inside EBITDA, requiring that split) was not used - Treatment A avoids needing an undisclosed split and matches the company's own net-debt presentation exactly. Lease liabilities are a modest 8.5% of total debt, so the treatment choice is not highly consequential here.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are attributable-to-members only: base_revenue, last_fcf and reported_fcf derive from the statutory 'Revenue and other income' and cash flow statement, which the NCI dividend line ($22m FY2026, file:8055) already nets out of the cash actually retained by members alongside the $255m dividend to members. NCI in the DCF is immaterial (~$14m FY2026 NCI share of profit on $238m group NPAT, ~6%) and is not separately deducted from the bridge to avoid double-counting; NOPAT in the model is not required to tie exactly to the $238m attributable NPAT since the model is built from EBITDA margins, not from reported NPAT downward.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (10-year, component-built), routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials' row, using owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (AUD-currency WACC, single lease treatment, no material NCI, no material non-operating income to strip). FRESH BUILD (no prior DCF/Drivers/memory entry for WOR.AX). Mid-cycle normalization approach: FY2026 was a trough year (underlying EBITA down 11% to $734m, margin 6.1% vs 6.8% FY2025, ~$58m Middle East conflict hit, gearing up to 26.4%, OCF nearly halved to $401m from $741m) following the April 2019 Jacobs ECR acquisition which roughly doubled revenue/share count (a structural break; pre-FY2020 history is not used to derive growth or margin paths). Underlying EBITA margin on STATUTORY (not aggregated) revenue has run 5.6%-7.3% over FY2022-FY2026 (avg ~6.4%); the EBITDA margin path used here (7.6% Y1 rising to a matured 8.3%) sits inside that historical band and below management's own 9.0-9.5% ex-procurement ambition, which is stated on a different (ex-procurement) revenue base and not taken at face value. FY2027 guidance (mid-to-high single-digit revenue and EBITA growth, H2-weighted) anchors Year 1 of the base case at 6% revenue growth. Buybacks ($166m FY2025, $359m FY2026, continuing under a new $300m program to May 2027) fund the flat share count assumed by the SBC-is-fully-expensed convention (section 1 of owner-fcf.md); SBC is small (~0.21% of revenue) so the flat-count convention costs little precision either way. Interest income ($16m FY2026) is NOT stripped from owner FCF because Worley carries net DEBT ($1,746m), not net cash - the interest-income-strip rule only applies when net cash exceeds ~1x the FCF base, which does not hold here; stripping it would double-penalize a company that is not net-cash. Shares outstanding (491m) = 487,660,203 on issue at 20 July 2026 (post FY2026 year-end, post continuing buyback; FY2026 Annual Report shareholder register, file:12305) plus ~3.4m weighted-average dilutive performance rights (file:9914), rounded. SBC-zero-market rule does not apply (SBC is present, just small); house and street bases are reported distinctly with an explicit small SBC path rather than degenerating to a point.

bear.narrative: Middle East disruption and second-order supply chain effects (sulphur supply, delayed FIDs) persist or recur beyond FY2027, and the guidance credibility problem repeats -- management underestimated the FY2026 Middle East EBITA hit twice (from $30-40m to $60m) during the year. Competitive EPCM tendering (Jacobs, Fluor, KBR, Bechtel, Wood Group and full-service entrants) compresses margin permanently below the historical average and the mix shifts toward lower-margin construction/fabrication/procurement work. Rising leverage (gearing 26.4% vs 20.9% FY2025) alongside a weaker operating cash flow ($401m vs $741m) constrains further buybacks, and a stronger AUD continues to be a translation headwind independent of operating performance. Revenue growth stalls near zero in real terms and margin never regains the FY2025 peak.

base.narrative: FY2027 guidance (mid-to-high single-digit revenue/EBITA growth, H2-weighted as Middle East volumes recover) is delivered roughly as stated, then decelerates toward a 2.5% terminal rate as the backlog ($13.8bn, +18% cc) converts to revenue at a normal pace. EBITDA margin recovers from the FY2026 Middle-East-depressed 7.5% toward a matured ~8.3% -- inside the historical 5.6-7.3%-of-statutory-revenue underlying-EBITA band once the ~$58m one-off conflict drag rolls off, but below management's own 9.0-9.5% ex-procurement ambition, which is not assumed to be fully achieved. Cash tax rate ramps from the FY2026 actual 22.8% toward 28% as the 'mix of foreign earnings' and non-deductible cost pressure management flagged (effective underlying rate already at 34.7%) works through. Working capital is a modest cash drag on growth (project-based receivables/WIP), not a tailwind.

bull.narrative: Middle East disruption resolves quickly through FY2027 as management expects, North American strength (largest market) broadens, and the growing major-projects pipeline (CP2 LNG both phases FID'd, INPEX Abadi, energy transition materials, data centers/nuclear/power in complex critical infrastructure) converts backlog into revenue faster than guided. The FY2030 'double-digit EBITA growth' medium-term ambition and the 9.0-9.5% ex-procurement margin target are substantially delivered as the $70m AI/digital investment and the cost-out program (already $132m vs $100m target) compound. WACC eased 1pp and terminal growth/cap nudged up to reflect a business proven to scale into higher-margin full-project-delivery work.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised above the 15% house default to 30% because Worley has twice underestimated and upgraded the Middle East EBITA impact within a single fiscal year (April 2026: $30-40m; June 2026: up to $60m) -- a live, demonstrated guidance-credibility problem, not a hypothetical risk -- and because gearing rose to 26.4% with operating cash flow nearly halved in the same year the buyback program continued, which is exactly the balance-sheet-flexibility risk section 3 of owner-fcf.md flags for an elevated bear weight. Bull weight trimmed to 25% because the FY2030 double-digit-EBITA and 9.0-9.5% ex-procurement margin ambitions require several distinct things to go right simultaneously (Middle East resolution, North American strength broadening, full-project-delivery scaling, AI investment payoff) rather than one lever. Base gets the remaining 45%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
